title: Boss 3: Scale or Kill? The ₹50,000 Reallocation
description: You are managing a ₹50,000/week budget for a high-growth brand. You have 4 live campaigns with completely different performance metrics. Evaluate the data, make the tough calls to Scale, Hold, or Kill, and defend your decisions to graduate as a Master Strategist!

steps.title: Step 1: Inspect the 4 Active Campaigns
steps.context: Review the last 14 days of performance across the 4 active campaigns in the account.
steps.question: Based on this data, which campaign is burning cash with virtually zero bottom-line return and should be killed immediately?
options: Campaign A
Campaign C
Campaign D (Traffic/Video views generating only 4 sales at ₹1,500 CPA and 0.6x ROAS)
Campaign B
steps.explain: Campaign D spent ₹6,000 with a catastrophic 0.6x ROAS and ₹1,500 CPA. Optimizing for video views instead of purchases wastes precious budget.
steps.hint: Look at which campaign has a ROAS below 1.0x and the highest CPA.

steps.title: Step 2: Diagnose Campaign B (High Frequency & Stagnation)
steps.context: Campaign B has a 2.1x ROAS (breakeven is 2.2x) and a Frequency of 4.6 with ₹387 CPA.
steps.question: What is the primary disease afflicting Campaign B?
options: Audience exhaustion and creative fatigue — high frequency (4.6) indicates the small interest pool is saturated with old creatives
The pixel has been uninstalled
The ad budget is 10 times too high
Meta is penalizing the brand for using Instagram
steps.explain: A frequency of 4.6 on a cold interest ad set causes creative fatigue, higher CPMs, and decaying conversion rates.
steps.hint: Check the frequency metric. Are the same people seeing this ad over 4 times?

steps.title: Step 3: Scaling Strategy for Campaign A
steps.context: Campaign A (Advantage+ Shopping) is your undisputed hero: 4.2x ROAS, low frequency (1.8), and stable CPA.
steps.question: How should you scale Campaign A's budget without shocking Meta's delivery algorithm into Learning Limited?
options: Increase the budget by 500% in one click at midnight
Scale the budget by 15% to 20% every 48 to 72 hours, monitoring CPA stability
Pause the campaign and recreate it with a ₹1,00,000 daily budget
Lower the budget so Meta gets desperate and gives cheaper clicks
steps.explain: Gradual vertical scaling (15-20% every 2-3 days) protects the learning algorithm from reset and maintains auction bid efficiency.

steps.title: Step 4: The ₹50,000 Budget Reallocation
steps.context: You killed Campaign D (₹6,000 freed) and pruned fatigued Ad Sets in Campaign B (₹4,000 freed). You have ₹10,000 in unlocked budget to reallocate for next week.
steps.question: Where is the smartest place to allocate this ₹10,000 freed capital?
options: Put ₹7,000 into scaling Campaign A (ASC) and ₹3,000 into a fresh Creative Sandbox testing new hooks
Put all ₹10,000 into Google Display Network
Spend it all on boosting TikTok posts
Put all ₹10,000 back into Campaign D to see if it turns around
steps.explain: Fueling your primary proven revenue engine (ASC) while reserving 20-30% for a dedicated creative testing sandbox guarantees both immediate cash flow and future creative pipeline.
steps.hint: Combine scaling the proven winner with continuous creative testing.

steps.title: Step 5: Creative Fatigue Prevention
steps.context: To keep Campaign A delivering at 4.2x ROAS as spend grows, you must supply it with fresh creatives.
steps.question: What is the best creative production cadence for a brand spending ₹50,000+ per week?
options: Wait 6 months until the client complains
Produce and test 3 to 5 new creative variations (new hooks, angles, formats) every week in a sandbox ad set before graduating winners to ASC
Never change the ad once it works
Rely solely on AI image generators without human review
steps.explain: High ad spend consumes audience attention fast. Testing 3-5 variations weekly ensures a continuous supply of winning assets.
steps.hint: Continuous creative iteration is the #1 lever for scaling.

steps.title: Step 6: The CEO Debrief Call
steps.context: The CEO asks: 'Why did you kill Campaign D? It had 45,000 video views! People were watching our brand!'
steps.question: How do you professionally answer in 'Client-Talk'?
options: Say: 'You don't understand marketing, leave me alone.'

Explain: 'While video views were high, only 4 views converted into paying customers at a ₹1,500 CPA. We redirected those funds into our top-converting campaign, driving 28 additional purchases at 4.2x ROAS and higher net profit.'
Apologize and immediately put all budget back into video views
Blame Mark Zuckerberg for the algorithm changes
steps.explain: Translating vanity metrics (video views) into business commercial realities (net profit and customer acquisition cost) demonstrates true CMO-level strategic acumen.
steps.hint: Focus on cash in the bank vs vanity views.
